title: scaffold-e2e's docker leg only exercises the --skip-install shape, so the pinned Dockerfile users actually get has no e2e coverage
body:
Observation found while implementing #9017 (PR #9115). Not a defect in that PR — recording it because the gap is invisible from either file alone.

## What is covered, and what is not

`.github/workflows/scaffold-e2e.yml` scaffolds with `--skip-install`:

```
node "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/packages/create-objectstack/bin/create-objectstack.js" e2e-app --skip-install --skip-skills
```

and the workflow then runs `npm install` itself, so the generated project is installed but the **scaffolder's own** post-install step never runs.

PR #9115 makes the scaffolder pin the Dockerfile's runtime image tag to the `@objectstack/cli` version the project resolved — and that pin happens **after** the scaffolder's install, which `--skip-install` suppresses. So:

- the shape the e2e builds and boots is the **unpinned** one (`FROM ghcr.io/objectstack-ai/objectstack:latest`);
- the shape a real `npx create-objectstack` user ships is the **pinned** one;
- the docker leg's own comment says it "exercises the exact Docker path a real `npm create objectstack` user ships", which is now true only of the `--skip-install` variant.

The pinned shape is covered by `packages/create-objectstack/src/runtime-image.test.ts`, which asserts on scaffolded output, so this is a missing **end-to-end** leg rather than an untested behaviour.

## Why it is not simply fixed in that PR

Letting the e2e scaffold without `--skip-install` is not a one-line swap: the workflow's install step carries the unpublished-version fallback (it rewrites the app's `@objectstack/*` ranges to `latest` when the repo version is not yet on the registry, then re-stamps `engines.protocol`), and moving the install into the scaffolder would move that fallback too. That is a deliberate design worth its own card rather than a rider.

## Possible shapes

- Scaffold a second, small project **without** `--skip-install` purely to assert the emitted Dockerfile is pinned — cheap, no docker build needed.
- Or teach the existing leg to run the scaffolder's install path, and relocate the unpublished-version fallback accordingly.

Neither is obviously right; the first is much cheaper and covers the actual regression risk (the pin silently not happening).

Related: #9017, PR #9115.
